QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_35

question.text: Maximum Drawdown (MDD) as a risk measure:

answer.text: Measures the total volatility of a fund's returns
Represents the peak-to-trough percentage decline in AUM over a period
Is the same as Value at Risk
Measures time to recovery from a loss

explanation.text: The Logic: Maximum Drawdown represents the peak-to-trough percentage decline in AUM over a specified reporting period. The workbook explicitly notes that MDD does not indicate recovery time. The Trap: Option A confuses MDD with total volatility (σ). Option C confuses it with VaR. Option D confuses it with time-to-recovery, which is a separate metric. Note: MDD captures the magnitude of the largest peak-to-trough loss; it does not, by itself, capture how long the fund takes to return to the prior peak.
